text:
Lena (Marketing): Quick sync — we need an updated battlecard + inbound routing rules for the launch webinar + benchmark post. Goal: one field cheat for SDRs, one-page battlecard for AE, and routing that channels higher-value leads to enterprise.
Arjun (Product): Agree. Core claims to test: serving-first perf, consistent behavior across hosted/dedicated/private, and cost controls (batching/cache/quantization). Need bench numbers vs big cloud AI APIs and infra vendors. Samir, can you validate the field-ready lines?
Samir (Sales): Yep. For SDRs let's standardize 3 quick rebuttals: 1) "Why not managed cloud endpoints?" -> predictable unit economics + rollout controls + private deployments. 2) "Why not self-host?" -> ops cost + kernel/config tradeoffs. 3) "What's the SLA?" -> point to Dedicated + Private tiers. I'll draft short soundbites.
Maya (Growth): Landing page CTA should route inbound to either 'webinar' or 'enterprise-demo' based on expected token usage and company size. Proposed pseudo-rule for ops to implement:
```
if (form.interest == 'webinar') route = 'webinar-funnel';
else if (company.size >= 1000 || est_monthly_tokens > 1e9) route = 'enterprise-demo';
else route = 'growth-nurture';
```
Simple and testable.
Jordan (AE): Also need a one-liner for AEs: "Choose Redwood when predictable latency, unit economics, and flexible deployment matter at scale." Can we tighten?
ops-bot: Reminder: webinar demo infra scheduled Thu 10:00 PST. Latest deploy: success. Logs: https://ci.redwood/deploy/524 (checks green).
Lena (Marketing): Owners: Arjun -> battlecard + microbench; Samir -> SDR cheat + objections; Maya -> routing implementation + landing copy; Jordan -> AE one-liners and opening script. Timeline: Drafts by Tue EOD, final by Wed. Any blockers?
Arjun (Product): I'll pull perf diffs: model_X on GCP endpoints vs Redwood-hosted vs Dedicated. ETA Mon noon with CSVs and a simple table. Will also include a note on quantization tradeoffs.
Samir (Sales): :thumbsup: I'll start the objection playbook. Can do procurement template and 3 short procurement FAQs.
Maya (Growth): Implementing rules in HubSpot. Test plan: 1) route webinar leads via 'interest' field, 2) flag high-token estimates to AE, 3) run A/B on CTA phrasing. I'll add mapping in the doc.
Lena (Marketing): Webinar narrative note: 10 min latency/cost story (customer-centric), 15 min live demo of fallbacks + dedicated. Slide idea: "When serving matters" with 3 bullets (latency, predictable cost, graceful degradation).
Jordan (AE): I'll draft an opening: "Most teams confuse model choice with serving. The real challenge is delivering consistent experience at scale — that's what we built Redwood for."
Lena (Marketing): I'll assemble draft doc and share here: https://docs.redwood/example-battlecard-draft — please comment directly.
Arjun (Product): Also add a microbenchmark table with header: [setup, seq_len, p95 latency, cost_per_1k_tokens]. Label the caveats: 'unit cost at 2k seq typical'.
Maya (Growth): Adding routing test cases to the doc now.
Lena (Marketing): Thanks everyone. Ping me if anything slips. :rocket:
